messages.text: Taylor ecstatic with Croke Park swansong

metadata.summary: Katie Taylor acclaimed becoming a three-time undisputed world champion in her farewell fight at Croke Park as the most special moment of her decorated career.
metadata.content: Katie Taylor ecstatic after beating Flora Pili to make perfect end to ‘dream career’ at Dublin's Croke Park | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Katie Taylor ecstatic after beating Flora Pili to make perfect end to ‘dream career’ at Dublin's Croke Park Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972. Sunday 6 September 2026 12:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the fight between Katie Taylor and Flora Pili Katie Taylor acclaimed becoming a three-time undisputed world champion in her farewell fight at Croke Park as the most special moment of her decorated career. Taylor outclassed Flora Pili in a unanimous points victory in front of a crowd of 80,000 to ensure her three decades as an amateur and professional boxer ended in fairytale fashion. Wild celebrations followed the announcement that she had overwhelmed the previously unbeaten Pili 100-90 100-90 98-91 on the scorecards. For Taylor the feeling of signing off in front of her fans bettered winning Olympic gold at London 2012, headlining Madison Square Garden and her trilogy against Amanda Serrano. Francis-Henri Graffard's star returns having not being seen since his third in the Prince Of Wales's Stakes - where there were excuses for the run given his misbehaviour in the stables prior to the race. That run is the only blemish to an otherwise seamless four-year-old campaign to date, which has seen him win the Prix Ganay & Prix Aga Khan IV, showing a devastating turn of foot in both. Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16. The 22-year-old will next face compatriot Iva Jovic for a quarter-final spot. "I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said.
